record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.context_brief: Round real-representable matroids with dual grid-cycle minors
record.original_question: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every round real-representable matroid with an M(G_n^+)^*-minor contains a U_{k,2k}-minor? Here G_n^+ is obtained by adding an apex vertex to an n by n grid, and M(G) denotes the cycle matroid of G.

evidence.quote: The graph G+ n is constructed by adding an apex vertex to an n × n grid.
Conjecture 10.3. For any positive integer k, there is an integer n such that, if M is a round R-representable matroid with an M(G+ n )∗-minor, then M contains a Uk,2k-minor.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G_n^+$ denote the graph obtained from the $n\times n$ grid graph by adding a single apex vertex adjacent to every vertex of the grid. For a graph $G$, let $M(G)$ denote its cycle matroid, and let $M^*$ denote the dual of a matroid $M$. A matroid $M$ is called round if it cannot be written as the union of two proper flats; equivalently, $M$ has no two disjoint cocircuits. A matroid is real-representable if it can be represented by a matrix over the real numbers. The uniform matroid $U_{k,2k}$ is the matroid on $2k$ elements whose independent sets are all subsets of size at most $k$.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $k$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that every round, real-representable matroid that contains $M(G_n^+)^*$ as a minor also contains $U_{k,2k}$ as a minor.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture about excluding uniform matroid minors in round real-representable matroids. A web search did not turn up any resolution of this specific conjecture; related literature discusses round matroids and grid-like matroid minors but does not announce a proof or disproof.
